summary: Justin Shimeld is a philosopher who completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania, where he was supervised by Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.

Justin Václav Prášek (1853–1924) was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and historical-archaeological studies. He earned his PhD at Charles University (~1872–1882) and studied at the universities of Munich and Berlin in 1885, later teaching Édouard Huber.
Justus Günther Grassmann (1779–1852) studied at the University of Halle (~1797–1801). He held a post at the Marienstiftsgymnasium from 1806 until 1852.

Justus Olshausen (1800–1882) was a linguist and scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He studied at Kiel, Berlin, and Paris under scholars including Silvestre de Sacy, and held posts at Kiel, Königsberg, and the Prussian Academy of Sciences.
Justyna Wiśniewska-Singh is an Indologist and linguist. She completed her MA and PhD at the University of Warsaw between 2001 and 2015, and held a post there in 2016.
Jvala Singh works in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia (2018–2024) and served as a lecturer at the University of California, Berkeley in 2021.
Jyotirindranath Tagore (1849–1925) was active in linguistics and other fields. He completed his education at the Hindu School and Presidency University (~1864–1865).

János Harmatta (1917–2004) was a linguist and scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He earned his PhD at Eötvös Loránd University, where he became Professor of Indo-European Linguistics, and held leadership posts at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences.

János Szerb (1951–1988) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Eötvös Loránd University and held posts at the University of Vienna (1982) and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (1984–1988).

Jérôme Ducor (born 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Lausanne and Geneva under Jacques May, later holding posts at the University of Lausanne, the University of Geneva, and the Musée d'ethnographie de Genève.

Józef Lączak (1926–1989) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Jagiellonian University under Helena Willman-Grabowska. He taught at Eötvös Loránd University, the University of Warsaw, and Helsinki, later heading the Indian Department at Jagiellonian University (1980–1989).

Józef Reczek (1936–1988) was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Jagiellonian University (1953–1959) under Jerzy Kuryłowicz, Tadeusz Pobożniak, and Tadeusz Milewski, becoming a docent there in 1972.

Józef Szczepan Kowalewski (1800–1878) worked in Iranian, Central Asian, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Vilnius and Kazan, later serving as professor and rector at Kazan State University and professor at the University of Warsaw.
Józef Turczyński (1884–1953) taught Constantin Régamey. He held posts at the Ukrainian National Academy of Music (~1915–1919) and the Chopin University of Music (~1920–1939).

József Budenz (1836–1892) was a linguist who studied at Marburg and Göttingen, where he was taught by Theodor Benfey. He worked as librarian at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences and was full professor at Eötvös Loránd University (1868–1892).
József Schmidt (1868–1933) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1886–1899) under Aurel Mayr, whom he succeeded, serving as a docent there from 1908 to 1920.

Jörg B. Quenzer (born 1961) works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He has held positions at the University of Hamburg (attested 2016 and 2026) and served on the editorial board of Studies in Manuscript Cultures (attested 2016).
Jörg Gengnagel is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held an apl. Prof. Dr. post at Heidelberg University (~2004–2018) and a post at the University of Würzburg (~2018).

Jörg Heimbel specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Tibet University and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2014), he has held posts at Hamburg, the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the University of Munich.
Jörg Plassen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He has held positions as professor at Geumgang University and Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2013).
